title: A Museum Label with Two Authors
title_ja: 二人の作者による展示解説
fact_notes: 人物・具体的な出来事は架空の思考実験・教材例。実在の調査・統計を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Imagine a small museum preparing an exhibition of handmade objects donated by people in the surrounding community.
sentences.ja: 周辺地域の人々が寄贈した手作り品の展示を準備する小さな博物館を想像しよう。

sentences.en: Among the objects is a woven basket that a retired shopkeeper used to carry vegetables home from the market.
sentences.ja: 展示品の中には引退した店主が市場から野菜を運ぶために使った編みかごがある。

sentences.en: A curator writes a label describing the material, technique, age, and physical condition of the basket.
sentences.ja: 学芸員はかごの素材、技法、年代、物理的状態を説明する解説を書く。

sentences.en: The information is accurate within the fictional example, but the donor feels that something significant is missing.
sentences.ja: 架空の例の中で情報は正確だが寄贈者は重要な何かが欠けていると感じる。

sentences.en: For the retired shopkeeper, the basket is associated with conversations she had with neighbors on the way to the market.
sentences.ja: 引退した店主にとってかごは市場へ向かう途中で近所の人と交わした会話と結びついている。

sentences.en: She remembers borrowing it from a relative and eventually learning to repair its handle herself.
sentences.ja: 親族から借り最終的に取っ手を自分で修理することを学んだと覚えている。

sentences.en: None of these memories can be inferred simply by examining the appearance of the object.
sentences.ja: これらの記憶はいずれも物の外見を調べるだけでは推測できない。

sentences.en: The curator realizes that technical descriptions and personal accounts can answer quite different questions about the same item.
sentences.ja: 学芸員は技術的記述と個人の話が同じ品について異なる問いに答え得ると気づく。

sentences.en: The museum decides to experiment with a label consisting of two clearly distinguished sections.
sentences.ja: 博物館は明確に区別した二つの部分からなる解説を試すことにする。

sentences.en: The first section describes the object using information that the museum can reasonably verify.
sentences.ja: 最初の部分は博物館が合理的に確認できる情報で物を記述する。

sentences.en: The second contains a short personal account attributed to the donor and published with her permission.
sentences.ja: 二つ目には寄贈者に帰属し本人の許可を得た短い個人の話を載せる。

sentences.en: The two sections are presented together without suggesting that every visitor must interpret the object in the same way.
sentences.ja: 来館者全員が同じ解釈をする必要があるとは示さず両方を一緒に提示する。

sentences.en: During a trial visit, some readers concentrate on the design and construction of the basket, while others become interested in its social history.
sentences.ja: 試験的な見学でかごの設計と作り方に集中する人も社会的歴史に関心を持つ人もいる。

sentences.en: The museum staff discuss whether the personal story might be mistaken for a complete account of everyday life in the entire community.
sentences.ja: 職員は個人の話が地域全体の日常生活の完全な説明と誤解されるかもしれないと話し合う。

sentences.en: They therefore identify the source of the testimony and avoid making claims that go beyond what the donor has actually described.
sentences.ja: そこで証言の出所を明示し寄贈者が実際に述べた内容を超える主張を避ける。

sentences.en: They also invite other contributors to share experiences that may differ from those presented in the exhibition.
sentences.ja: 展示された経験とは異なるかもしれない経験をほかの提供者に共有するよう促す。

sentences.en: The example illustrates that an object can have several kinds of significance without those meanings necessarily contradicting one another.
sentences.ja: この例は物が複数の意味を持っても、それらが必ずしも矛盾しないことを示す。

sentences.en: A description of its physical features and an account of its personal use can complement each other.
sentences.ja: 物理的特徴の記述と個人的な使用の話は補い合える。

sentences.en: However, distinguishing the evidence supporting each description remains an essential part of responsible interpretation.
sentences.ja: しかし各記述を支える根拠を区別することは責任ある解釈に欠かせない。

sentences.en: The basket becomes meaningful not because one author controls its story, but because several perspectives are carefully brought into conversation.
sentences.ja: かごは一人の作者が物語を支配するのでなく、複数の視点が慎重に対話に持ち込まれることで意味を持つ。

questions.prompt: What did the curator first describe?
options: The names of all market visitors.

questions.prompt: What does the donor associate with the basket?
options: Conversations on the way to the market.
questions.explanation_ja: 市場へ行く途中の会話。

options: Personal experiences cannot necessarily be inferred from physical features.
The object has no visible features.
The curator cannot see the basket.
questions.explanation_ja: 物の外見だけでは経験は分からない。

questions.prompt: What did the second label section contain?
options: A universal history of the town.
They present different kinds of information and evidence.
The object can have only one meaning.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる情報の種類を区別。

options: Visitors might read the date incorrectly in every case.
The basket might become a photograph.
A personal story might be mistaken for a complete community history.
The donor had never used the basket.
questions.explanation_ja: 一人の話を地域全体と誤解する可能性。

questions.prompt: How did staff address that concern?
options: Identified the source and avoided unsupported claims.
questions.explanation_ja: 出所を明示し根拠を超えない。

options: A museum must use only technical labels.
Every memory represents an entire society.
The physical object alone reveals all meanings.
Several perspectives can enrich an exhibit when their sources are distinguished.
questions.explanation_ja: 根拠を区別した複数の視点が理解を豊かにする。

grammar.focus: can be inferred simply by examining
grammar.explanation_ja: can be＋過去分詞で可能性の受動態、by＋動名詞は手段。
canは可能性、each otherは相互関係。

paraphrases.rewrite: Merely looking at the object cannot reveal those personal memories.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 外見だけでは記憶は分からない。

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同意を得て出所を示す。
